hook: A single-page monochrome still image captured by a U.S. military sensor system, submitted by the FBI to AARO as a UAP report, showing a central crosshair reticle over an indistinct background that may be a mountain range in the Western United States.
why_it_matters: This image represents the FBI's formal UAP reporting pipeline to AARO, demonstrating interagency coordination on anomaly documentation as mandated by recent disclosure requirements. The operator's explicit inability to positively identify the object, combined with the image's pre-submission redaction and absence of an accompanying mission report, limits what AARO could assess. The incorrect system timestamp further undermines the evidentiary value of the record.
key_findings: The image was captured by a U.S. military system and submitted by the FBI to AARO, indicating cross-agency UAP reporting channels are active as of 2025.
The original imagery was altered with redactions before submission to AARO, meaning AARO received an incomplete version of the source material.
No accompanying mission report was provided, leaving the operational context — flight path, sensor parameters, crew observations — unrecorded in this file.
The embedded date in the image is acknowledged to be incorrect due to system clock misconfiguration, removing timestamp reliability as an analytical anchor.
The operator on record explicitly could not positively identify the UAP, establishing this as an unresolved case with no official attribution.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The document was formally submitted by the FBI to AARO as part of the mandated UAP reporting process, making AARO the direct recipient and intended resolver of this case.

The image originated from a U.S. military system and was routed through the FBI rather than intelligence collection channels, but the redaction of the source imagery before submission suggests some access-control or classification consideration.
